name: Furanylfentanyl
metabolism: Four breakdown products were found in 500 urine samples from people who had taken opioids. The strongest signal came from the hydrolysis product 4-ANPP and its sulphate form, found in 42 of the 51 samples that were positive for furanylfentanyl; a product formed when the furanyl ring picks up two extra hydrogens turned up in 86% of cases. The version with the alkyl group taken off, norfuranylfentanyl, was found in only four positive cases, which suggests that swapping the amide-linked group for a furanyl carboxamide pushes the breakdown towards hydrolysis. Lab work with human liver microsomes found seven products; one of the main ones, nortetrahydrofuranylfentanyl, comes from taking the alkyl group off and works well as a marker that furanylfentanyl was taken. The hydroxylated forms were also found in plenty of blood and urine samples taken after death.
summary: Furanylfentanyl is a fentanyl analogue and opioid analgesic that has been sold as a designer drug.
